title: A young spinner at Mollahan Mills
subject: hine-labor
creator: Lewis Wickes Hine

date.label: 3 December 1908
date.note: Hine’s caption card dates the photograph to 3 December 1908.

material: Digitized photographic print from a glass-negative photograph
alt: A young girl stands beside a long row of spinning machinery in a cotton mill.
caption: Hine’s photograph and caption record different kinds of evidence. The overseer’s denial is reported by Hine; hours and age cannot be read directly from the image.
notice: Compare the person’s height with the machinery.
What can the image show without its caption?
rights: Library of Congress records no known restrictions on publication. The National Child Labor Committee placed no restrictions on use of the Hine material when donating the collection.
credit: Lewis Wickes Hine. National Child Labor Committee collection, Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division. Hine 358; LC-DIG-nclc-01451.
relevance: Work, reform and the different evidentiary roles of a photograph and its caption.

alt: Liberty presents a sword marked Service to a younger woman; a shield names State and National Councils of Defense.
caption: A 1917 wartime recruiting appeal. Persuasive language is evidence of the desired response, not proof of actual participation.
notice: Which response does the poster seek?
